stories.headline: UBTECH starts the world's first 10,000-unit humanoid robot factory in Liuzhou, China

key_facts.fact: UBTECH began production on September 12, 2026 at its Industrial Humanoid Robot Super Smart Factory in Liuzhou, Guangxi, the first plant designed for annual capacity above 10,000 humanoids
key_facts.excerpt: UBTECH (09880.HK) officially commenced production at its industrial humanoid robot super smart factory in Liuzhou, Guangxi, on September 12, making it the world's first manufacturing base of its kind with an annual planned capacity exceeding 10,000 units.

key_facts.fact: The plant covers 14,000 square meters with 13.8-meter ceilings and is designed to roll out one finished robot every 10 minutes, building Walker S and Cruzr series machines on a mixed-model line
key_facts.excerpt: The facility spans 14,000 square meters and primarily produces Walker S Series and Cruzr Series embodied intelligence industrial humanoid robots, with one complete unit rolling off the line every 10 minutes.

key_facts.fact: The factory was built with Siemens Digital Industries Software using digital-twin simulation and the Yanshee MOM manufacturing operations system, in a 'robots build robots' layout
key_facts.excerpt: The factory was built through deep collaboration with Siemens, incorporating digital twin technology and the Yanshee MOM manufacturing operations management system to achieve a flexible mixed-line production model where 'robots build robots.'

key_facts.fact: UBTECH's Hong Kong-listed shares rose more than 3% on September 14, reaching HK$80.4 on HK$125 million of turnover
key_facts.excerpt: The production launch news drove UBTECH's Hong Kong-listed shares up more than 3% in early trading on the 14th, reaching a high of HK$80.4 with turnover of HK$ 125 million.

key_facts.fact: UBTECH's full-size humanoid revenue rose 1,445% in the first half of 2026 on 921 bipedal deliveries, and the company is targeting a unit cost below $20,000
key_facts.excerpt: The expansion comes on the heels of UBTECH's 1,445% revenue surge in full-size humanoids in H1 2026, backing its bid to cut production costs below $20,000.

key_facts.fact: Assembling one humanoid chassis requires driving more than 2,000 screws across 50 specifications, logged by automated torque stations feeding the factory's digital backbone
key_facts.excerpt: Assembling a single humanoid chassis requires driving more than 2,000 screws across 50 distinct specifications. Automated digital torque stations feed fasteners, monitor driving depth, and stream real-time torque-angle telemetry directly into the factory floor's digital backbone

key_facts.fact: Chinese state media said the plant, opened on Saturday, can produce 10,000 industrial humanoids a year with a robot leaving the line every 10 minutes
key_facts.excerpt: A super smart factory capable of producing 10,000 industrial humanoid robots annually was put into operation on Saturday in Liuzhou, China. Here, a robot can roll off the line every 10 minutes.

stories.headline: Samsung and SK hynix reject KEPCO's $18.6 billion power-bill prepayment for chip-cluster grids

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix told state utility KEPCO on September 14 that they would not prepay a combined 25 trillion won (about $18.6 billion) of electricity bills
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's two major chipmakers, Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc., have rejected a proposal from state-run Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) to prepay five years' worth of electricity bills, industry sources said Monday.

key_facts.fact: KEPCO had asked Samsung for 20 trillion won ($14.8 billion) and SK hynix for 5 trillion won, roughly five years of each company's bills based on last year's payments
key_facts.excerpt: Debt-ridden KEPCO recently proposed that Samsung Electronics pay 20 trillion won (US$14.8 billion) and SK hynix pay 5 trillion won in advance, amounts equivalent to roughly five years of electricity bills based on the companies' payments last year, they said.

key_facts.fact: The chipmakers concluded after internal reviews that they could not lock up the cash on the assumption the AI-driven memory boom would last five years, and cited the need to fund fabs and R&D
key_facts.excerpt: they concluded it would be difficult to lock up funds on the assumption that the current upturn will last five years. They also cited the need to secure funds for medium- to long-term investments such as factory expansions and research and development.

key_facts.fact: KEPCO confirmed both companies rejected the plan, which would have funded transmission and substation build-out for the Yongin semiconductor cluster and the Honam region
key_facts.excerpt: Kepco confirmed that both companies had rejected the proposal. ... It planned to use the funds to prioritize expansion of the national power grid, accelerating construction of transmission and substation networks in areas expected to see heavy electricity demand, such as the Yongin semiconductor cluster currently under construction.

key_facts.fact: The structure would have functioned as a loan: interest above the two-year government bond yield, with principal and interest deducted from the companies' power bills every six months
key_facts.excerpt: It had also proposed paying interest above the yield on two-year government bonds on the prepaid amount, with the principal and interest to be deducted from the companies' electricity bills every six months going forward. In effect, the structure would have the chipmakers lend Kepco money and recoup it later through their power bills.

key_facts.fact: KEPCO's total debt stood at 210.7 trillion won at the end of June, with daily interest expenses of about 11.5 billion won
key_facts.excerpt: As of the end of June, KEPCO's total debt stood at 210.7 trillion won, and its daily interest expenses reached 11.5 billion won.

key_facts.fact: The prepayment would have covered 2027 to 2031 and was calculated from 2025 bills of 4.1 trillion won for Samsung and 900 billion won for SK hynix
key_facts.excerpt: This amount was calculated based on the electricity bills paid by the two companies last year—4.1 trillion won for Samsung Electronics and 900 billion won for SK Hynix—covering a five-year period from 2027 to 2031.

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed data center builder Firmus seeks up to $5 billion in an Australian IPO

key_facts.fact: Firmus Technologies is seeking to raise up to $5 billion in an IPO it aims to launch in October, with an ASX debut as early as late October
key_facts.excerpt: Australian AI infrastructure company Firmus Technologies is seeking to raise up to $5 billion in its initial public offering, aiming to launch next month, two people with knowledge of the matter said.

key_facts.fact: At $5 billion the deal would be the fourth-largest IPO globally this year behind SpaceX, CXMT and Cerebras Systems, and the second-largest Australian listing ever after Telstra's $10 billion float in 1997
key_facts.excerpt: At $5 billion, the IPO would rank as the fourth-largest globally so far this year, behind SpaceX, CXMT Corp and Cerebras Systems, according to Dealogic data. It would also be the second-largest Australia-listed IPO on record, behind only Telstra Corp's $10 billion flotation in 1997.

key_facts.fact: The Australian Financial Review first reported on Monday that Firmus was in talks to raise up to A$7 billion; Bloomberg also reported the size
key_facts.excerpt: The Australian Financial Review was first to report on Monday that Firmus was in discussions to raise up to A$7 billion ($5 billion) through its IPO. Bloomberg News also reported the potential size of the offering.

key_facts.fact: Firmus's valuation passed $10.5 billion in August, up from $5.5 billion in April, and its backers include Nvidia and Blackstone
key_facts.excerpt: The figure the company was working with in April was $2bn, at a valuation of $5.5bn. By August the valuation had passed $10.5bn. ... Its backers now include Nvidia and Blackstone, and the question the roadshow will settle is whether a $10.5bn valuation is a judgement on 900MW of contracts or on the two sites currently drawing power.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Singapore, Firmus started as a bitcoin miner; investor meetings began in mid-September with Australian roadshows to follow
key_facts.excerpt: Investor meetings began in the middle of this month, with Australian roadshows to follow. No pricing, listing date or free float has been announced. The company was founded in 2019 and headquartered in Singapore, and it started out mining Bitcoin.

key_facts.fact: The sale will test investor appetite for AI data-center builders just as industry leaders warn the pace of AI investment may be hard to sustain
key_facts.excerpt: The planned share sale would test investor appetite for companies building the data centres and related systems that provide computing power for artificial intelligence, even as some industry leaders warn that the rapid pace of investment and model development may be difficult to sustain.

stories.headline: Hisense-controlled optical chipmaker Ligent files for a $723 million Hong Kong IPO

key_facts.fact: Ligent Technologies filed with the Hong Kong exchange on Monday to raise HK$5.67 billion ($723 million), offering 172 million shares at HK$32.96 each
key_facts.excerpt: China's Ligent Technologies is looking to raise HK$5.67 billion ($723.02 million) through an initial public offering in Hong Kong, according to a filing with the exchange on Monday. The optical communications equipment maker is offering 172 million shares at an offer price of HK$32.96 apiece.

key_facts.fact: Shares are slated to start trading in Hong Kong on September 22
key_facts.excerpt: The company's shares are slated to debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange on September 22.

key_facts.fact: Cornerstone investors committed $340 million, or 47% of the base deal, and the offer price implies a market value of HK$32.4 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The maker of fibre optic communications equipment has received US$340 million from cornerstone investors, or 47 percent of the base share sale, the prospectus showed. ... Ligent has offered 172 million shares at an offer price of HK$32.96 apiece, equivalent to a market value of HK$32.4 billion

key_facts.fact: The company is controlled by Chinese conglomerate Hisense Group and makes optical transceivers, optical chips and network terminals used in data centers and cloud computing
key_facts.excerpt: Ligent, controlled by Chinese technology conglomerate Hisense Group Holding ... Ligent makes optical transceivers, optical chips and network terminals. Its products are used in data centres, cloud computing and telecommunications networks.

key_facts.fact: Ligent's own filing says it held a 4.0% share of global optical-module revenue in 2025, fifth among specialist makers, and is one of the first Chinese suppliers to mass-produce 800G and 1.6T modules, with 3.2T and 6.4T engines in development
key_facts.excerpt: 2025年，按全球光模塊收入計，我們佔有4.0%的市場份額，在全球所有專業光模塊廠商中排名第五 ... 我們是中國首批成功開發並批量生產800G及1.6T光模塊的光模塊廠商之一。我們積極研究下一代3.2T光模塊及6.4T光引擎。

key_facts.fact: Proceeds will fund R&D and production capacity expansion, with the company citing AI training and inference networks as the growth driver
key_facts.excerpt: It said it will use IPO proceeds to fund research and development, expand production capacity and support general corporate purposes.

stories.headline: TSMC maps 2027 expansion: 2nm capacity up 22% by mid-2027, CoWoS packaging to double by 2028

key_facts.fact: TSMC has for the first time outlined 2027 expansion targets, with 2nm capacity set to grow 22% and 3nm more than 16% between end-2026 and mid-2027, according to Taiwan's Economic Daily News
key_facts.excerpt: The Economic Daily News, citing supply chain sources, reports that TSMC has for the first time outlined its 2027 expansion targets, with 2nm capacity set to grow 22% and 3nm more than 16% from end-2026 to mid-2027.

key_facts.fact: 2nm output is expected to rise from 90,000 wafers per month at end-2026 to 110,000 by mid-2027, while 3nm goes from more than 180,000 to 210,000 wafers per month
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC's 2nm capacity is expected to jump from 90,000 wafers per month at end-2026 to 110,000 by mid-2027, according to the Economic Daily News. The 3nm ramp is equally aggressive, rising from more than 180,000 to 210,000 wafers per month over the same period

key_facts.fact: TSMC is adding three 3nm fabs across Taiwan, Arizona and Japan and converting 5nm tooling in Taiwan to add more 3nm capacity
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is adding three 3nm fabs across Taiwan, Arizona and Japan, while continuing to convert 5nm equipment in Taiwan to support additional 3nm capacity, the Economic Daily News reports.

key_facts.fact: CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity, the bottleneck for AI accelerators, could double from roughly 130,000 wafers per month at end-2026 to 260,000 by end-2028, centered on AP7 in Taiwan and the Arizona campus
key_facts.excerpt: CoWoS capacity could double from roughly 130,000 wafers per month by end-2026 to 260,000 by end-2028. The ramp is expected to center on AP7 in Taiwan and the Arizona campus, where local packaging would reduce the need to ship advanced chips back to Taiwan

key_facts.fact: TSMC guided 2026 capital spending of $60 billion to $64 billion on its July earnings call, with 70%-80% going to advanced process technologies, as 3nm is poised to overtake 5nm as its largest revenue contributor
key_facts.excerpt: At the earnings call in July, TSMC said its 2026 capital spending would range between $60 billion and $64 billion, with about 70%–80% allocated to advanced process technologies.

sources.title: TSMC Reportedly Targets 22% 2nm, 16%+ 3nm Capacity Boost by Mid-2027; CoWoS to Double by 2028
